clue.text: Vance hopes perhaps to obtain Rodin's first Thinker

parts.note: Philo Vance is S. S. Van Dine's detective, so his first name stands for Vance

indicators.note: perhaps marks the letters of hopes as only one possible arrangement, so they are rearranged
first asks for only the opening letter of the word Rodin's

explanation.surface: A man called Vance hopes to get hold of Rodin's original sculpture, The Thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rodin's first Thinker' points at the famous statue, but Thinker alone is the definition; 'perhaps' rearranges HOPES into SOPHE, and 'first' takes R from Rodin's.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep reasoner devoted to wisdom and ideas is a thinker by profession.

clue.text: Great fear of seeing one in a movie

indicators.note: in places the word for one within the slang word for a film

parts.note: a pic is informal for a film or movie
an means one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone is terrified at the prospect of watching themselves in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seeing' tempts as part of the mechanism, but 'of seeing' is only linking; 'in' is the container signal, and pic is informal slang for a film.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden overwhelming terror is the commonest sense of the word.

clue.text: One like Sassoon as child and adult penning lines

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the child-and-adult pair holds the lines between them

parts.note: an infant is a young child
a man is a grown-up male
RY, short for railway, is the usual crossword abbreviation for lines

explanation.surface: Someone resembling the war poet Sassoon, both as a boy and grown up, writing verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Siegfried Sassoon fought in the trenches of the First World War; 'penning lines' suggests writing poetry, but 'penning' means enclosing and lines are railway lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassoon served as a foot soldier's officer on the Western Front, a soldier of the foot regiments.

clue.text: Musical that's fine if abridged

parts.note: a Rodgers and Hammerstein stage show named after a US state, whose two-letter postal abbreviation is the word meaning fine or all right

explanation.surface: A stage show that works well once it has been cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: Abridged means abbreviated: the state's postal code is OK, which means fine.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rodgers and Hammerstein stage show of 1943, and a US state whose abbreviation is OK.

clue.text: Dahl's uncle, a reeve or steward

definitions.meaning: Roald Dahl wrote the adult novel My Uncle ...
the Reeve in Chaucer's Canterbury Tales is named ...
in King Lear, Goneril's steward is called ...

explanation.surface: Roald Dahl's uncle worked as a reeve or steward on an estate.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: Dahl's novel My Uncle Oswald, Chaucer's Reeve, and Goneril's steward in King Lear. A reeve was a manor's overseer.
explanation.definitionFit: The same first name belongs to Dahl's fictional uncle, Chaucer's pilgrim Reeve and Shakespeare's servant in Lear.

clue.text: Solo Chinese dynasty

definitions.meaning: ... Solo is the smuggler pilot in Star Wars
the dynasty ruling China from 206 BC to AD 220

explanation.surface: A Chinese dynasty that stood alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solo' looks like an adjective describing the dynasty, but it is Han Solo of Star Wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Star Wars pilot's first name and the imperial house that ruled China for four centuries.

clue.text: Artist, F Astaire, mostly dancing with ethereal movement

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the stock abbreviation for an artist

indicators.note: dancing sets the letters moving into a new order, apt for the dancer named
mostly means nearly all of the words F Astaire are used, dropping their final letter

explanation.surface: An artist and Fred Astaire glide across the floor with airy grace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the final E of the dancer's name, and 'dancing' rearranges the seven remaining letters into STAFARI. RA stands for Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jamaican religious and spiritual movement, ethereal standing in for spiritual or otherworldly.

clue.text: Poke around hospital with a girl, a screenwriter

indicators.note: around puts the poke word round the hospital letter

parts.note: to poke is to jab
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
Val is a girl's name, short for Valerie

explanation.surface: Someone pokes about a hospital with a girl, who turns out to be a screenwriter.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth Prawer Jhabvala wrote the Merchant Ivory screenplays; the clue's 'a girl' gives A after VAL in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth Prawer Jhabvala won Oscars for writing films such as A Room with a View.

clue.text: Pitt's brother, a democrat

definitions.note: the definition names the forename belonging to the actor surnamed Pitt

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for a US Democrat

explanation.surface: William Pitt's brother was a member of the Democratic party.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the Prime Minister Pitt, but it is the actor Brad Pitt; his first name is what belongs to Pitt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hollywood actor surnamed Pitt has this forename.

clue.text: The amount of dust raised by Waugh — a pain in the neck

definitions.text: The amount of dust raised by Waugh
definitions.meaning: Evelyn Waugh's novel is titled A ... of Dust
an unruly or troublesome person or child is called this

explanation.surface: Waugh kicks up some dust and is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: Evelyn Waugh's 1934 novel is A Handful of Dust; a difficult child is 'a bit of a handful'.
explanation.definitionFit: As much as one fist holds, from Waugh's title, and also a troublesome person.

clue.text: Barbara — a name that may be followed by Castle

definitions.meaning: Barbara ... was a British actress of the Carry On films and EastEnders

definitions.text: a name that may be followed by Castle
definitions.meaning: the royal residence in Berkshire, west of London

explanation.surface: A woman called Barbara bears a name that a castle can follow.
explanation.walkthrough: Barbara Windsor was a British comic actress; Windsor Castle is the royal residence west of London. 'Barbara Castle' was also a Labour minister, a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Surname of the actress Barbara and the town whose royal fortress is famous.

clue.text: 1A returning without a taxi

indicators.note: returning sends the phrase for lacking a taxi back the other way, read right to left

parts.note: having no cab, no taxi

explanation.surface: A thinker comes home without hailing a taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: Francis Bacon was the Elizabethan essayist and natural philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon, Elizabethan essayist and pioneer of scientific method, was a renowned thinker.

clue.text: Visionary composer and 1A, his girl Friday?

definitions.meaning: the medieval abbess of Bingen had visions, wrote music and wrote philosophy
in the film His Girl Friday the reporter Hildy Johnson's full first name is this

explanation.surface: A composer with visions and a thinker, and his assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: Hildegard of Bingen was a 12th-century mystic, composer and thinker; in the 1940 film His Girl Friday the heroine is Hildy, short for Hildegard. A 'girl Friday' is a female assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: The twelfth-century abbess saint of Bingen, mystic and polymath, shares her forename with the film's heroine Hildy.

clue.text: "This work will ask as many more officials, to make —— s and expunctions" (Milton)

definitions.text: "This work will ask as many more officials, to make —— s and expunctions" (Milton)

parts.words: "This work will ask as many more officials, to make —— s and expunctions" (Milton)
parts.note: a quotation from Milton's Areopagitica, attacking licensing of books; the blank is a word for cleansing a text of offensive matter, partnering expunctions

explanation.surface: A line from Milton's prose arguing that censorship would need an army of officials.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the blank in Milton's Areopagitica (1644): the missing word, plus the printed s, means censorings by cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing objectionable passages from a book is censorship by cutting, paired by Milton with deletions.

clue.text: Ars magna perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps flags the Latin phrase as one rearrangement among many of the same letters

explanation.surface: Is 'the great art' a fair description?
explanation.walkthrough: Ars magna, Latin for 'great art', is itself a rearrangement of the answer, so the clue is both wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearranged letters of a word or phrase, of which the Latin is itself an instance.

clue.text: Ace staff, capital, seen around a base in Warner's work

indicators.note: seen around says the ace-staff-capital chain is wrapped round the base

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace
a rod is a staff or stick
Rome is the capital of Italy
e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

explanation.surface: A top officer with a staff in the capital stands round a military base in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Rex Warner's 1941 novel is The Aerodrome; 'seen around' wraps the ace-staff-capital chain round E, the mathematical base, which sits just after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: Rex Warner's novel The Aerodrome is about an air force base, and this is its title.

clue.text: A French dish with a touch of oregano for a 1A

parts.note: plat is French for dish

indicators.note: a touch of takes only a trace, the first letter, of the word oregano

explanation.surface: A French dish seasoned with a pinch of oregano is served to a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek thinker of the Academy; 'A French dish' is the French word plat.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian pupil of Socrates is the archetypal Greek thinker.

clue.text: Buxtehude, say, composing a strong introduction to introit

indicators.note: composing means arranging, so the letters are put together in a new order, apt for music
introduction to takes the opening letter of the word introit

explanation.surface: The composer Buxtehude writes a powerful opening to the introit.
explanation.walkthrough: Dieterich Buxtehude was a Baroque organist at Lübeck; 'composing' rearranges ASTRONG plus I (the start of introit). An introit is the opening chant of the Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: Buxtehude was the celebrated church keyboard player at Lübeck whom Bach walked miles to hear.

clue.text: So, a brute that's vandalized, like Frank Fry

indicators.note: vandalized means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A brute has smashed things up, just like a character called Frank Fry.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank Fry is the villain of Hitchcock's 1942 film Saboteur, who sets fire to an aircraft factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Fry, Hitchcock's villain, wrecks war production, a wrecker for an enemy.

clue.text: Stoker preceded by a patriarch

indicators.note: preceded by puts the single letter before the novelist's first name

parts.note: Bram Stoker wrote Dracula

explanation.surface: A Stoker, a man who fuels furnaces, comes before the patriarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Stoker is Bram Stoker, author of Dracula, not someone feeding a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham's original name in Genesis, the founding father of the Israelites.

clue.text: Like Mahler's 4th introduced by a composer using a stave?

indicators.note: introduced by puts the composer first, before the key-signature phrase

parts.note: Sir Hubert Parry was the English composer of Jerusalem
Mahler's Fourth Symphony is in G major, so it is in G

explanation.surface: A composer introduces something resembling Mahler's Fourth, written on a musical stave.
explanation.walkthrough: Stave looks musical, but it is a wooden staff used to ward off blows; Hubert Parry was an English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fending off a blow with a staff is warding it off, so the question mark flags the weapon sense.

clue.text: Term used to identify Mantel

definitions.meaning: the Oxford and Dublin spring term is called this
the first name of the novelist Mantel, author of Wolf Hall

explanation.surface: A word used to identify the novelist Mantel.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford's spring term is Hilary term; Hilary Mantel wrote the Wolf Hall trilogy.
explanation.definitionFit: The forename of the Wolf Hall novelist, and the name of the university's spring session.

clue.text: In a state, with nation upset, we have slowish movement

parts.note: ND is the abbreviation for North Dakota

indicators.note: upset knocks the letters of nation over into a new order

explanation.surface: In a country where the nation is in turmoil, we find a slow passage of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the letters of nation into ANTINO; 'In ... we have' is the frame linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tempo marking a little quicker than a walking pace, used for a section of a piece.

clue.text: 1A? Yes, right

parts.note: aye means yes

explanation.surface: Asked if they are a thinker, someone says yes, right.
explanation.walkthrough: A. J. Ayer was the British logical positivist, author of Language, Truth and Logic.
explanation.definitionFit: A. J. Ayer was a prominent twentieth-century Oxford thinker.

clue.text: Berg — a large boat initially hit one

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word boat

parts.note: an means one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An iceberg: a large boat hit one at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Berg suggests an iceberg, but it is the composer Alban Berg; 'hit' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was the Austrian composer of Wozzeck, so his forename stands for him.

clue.text: Be about to annoy, we hear, 1A

indicators.note: about places the word Be around the sound for annoy
we hear signals that the annoy word is spelt by how it is said

parts.note: to irk is to annoy

explanation.surface: Someone is about to irritate, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmund Burke was the Irish-born statesman and political thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Burke, author of Reflections on the Revolution in France, was a political thinker.

clue.text: One raced about me on the way back. Say, who would have thought it?

definitions.text: Say, who would have thought it?

indicators.note: on the way back sends the whole assembly in the opposite direction
about puts the one-and-raced pair round the word me

parts.note: a means one
tore means raced, rushed

explanation.surface: Someone races round on the return journey, exclaiming that nobody expected it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an example ('Say'); 'about' puts the one-and-raced pair round the word me, giving AMETORE, and 'on the way back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhetorical question, asked for effect with no reply expected, of which 'who would have thought it?' is an example.

clue.text: Character turning up in Oil! eventually

indicators.note: turning up in a down entry means the hidden letters are read upwards
in shows the letters are found within the run of words Oil! eventually

explanation.surface: A character appears late on in Upton Sinclair's novel Oil!
explanation.walkthrough: Oil! is Upton Sinclair's novel, filmed as There Will Be Blood, where the preacher is Eli.
explanation.definitionFit: Eli is a figure in Sinclair's novel and its film adaptation, a person in the story.

clue.text: One in car about to enter Eastern section; they prefer to fly

indicators.note: to enter puts the car-and-about group inside the Eastern-section pair

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for section, as in statutes

indicators.note: in sets the one letter inside the car make

parts.note: MG is a British car make
one is the Roman numeral I
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A passenger in a car enters the eastern part of town, though they would rather fly.
explanation.walkthrough: Fly here means flee: exiles who left their homeland. MG is a British sports car.
explanation.definitionFit: Exiles who have left their country chose flight over staying.

clue.text: Ellis, who had no coward soul

definitions.meaning: Ellis Bell was the pseudonym under which she published
her poem begins No coward soul is mine

explanation.surface: Ellis, a person who was never a coward.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brontës wrote as Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell; the poem No Coward Soul Is Mine was her last.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Wuthering Heights wrote under a pen name and wrote the poem of courageous faith.
